name: Second-Key
description: A two-person check a family runs before an elderly relative sends money to someone new.

paragraphs: A two-person check a family runs before an elderly relative sends money to someone new. A trusted family member, the second key, calls them back and reads out a release code.
Try it: two phones side by side · the app on your own phone · Video (2:11):

A bank never lets one person move a large sum to a new beneficiary alone. It applies dual control, and it calls back on a number it already holds. Families have neither, and fraudsters work on exactly that gap: in France, manipulation fraud reached €516 million in 2025, up 34% in a year, and the fake bank adviser who asks for a transfer to a "safe account" is its most frequent form (Banque de France, OSMP annual report 2025).
features: Pairing, once, in the same room. The parent's phone shows a QR code; the second key's camera opens it. Both phones keep the same secret and show the same three check words.

A request in four questions. Before paying someone new, the parent enters the amount and the payee, says who the payee is, and answers four yes/no questions. The request goes to the second key by text message.
A briefing for the call. The second key sees the request and the scam script the answers match, for example "The fake bank adviser", with the questions to ask.
A call-back on the saved number. The second key calls the parent on the number saved at pairing. If they agree, they read a six-digit code aloud.
The key turns, or the payment stops. The parent types the code. If the second key refuses, the parent's screen says: do not send the money, hang up, call your bank on the number on your card.
